How to make your weekends
feel longer
Start Saturday early. Waking up at a normal time instead of noon gives you four extra hours. Those morning hours feel like a whole bonus day.
Do something new every weekend. A new place, a new dish, a new activity. Your brain remembers new experiences as longer than routine ones.
Get the boring tasks done Friday evening. Laundry, groceries, emails. Starting the weekend with nothing on your list feels like freedom.
Go outside for real. A hike, a day by the sea, a trip to a nearby town. Time in nature makes days feel bigger and slower.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Saturday mornings feel richer when they start with something interesting.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Saturday mornings feel richer when they start with something interesting.

slides.texte_overlay: Limit your screen time. Hours of scrolling blur together and disappear. Put the phone away and the weekend suddenly stretches.
Protect Sunday evening. A calm dinner, a short plan for Monday, an early night. Ending well makes the whole weekend feel complete.
